stem: A 31-year-old patient with immune thrombocytopenia receives corticosteroid treatment and the platelet count rises. In a hypothetical model, the treatment suppresses the platelet-directed immune process without directly changing platelet production. Which of the following paired changes best explains the response?

options.label: A
options.text: Shorter platelet survival; unchanged platelet production
options.explanation: Shortening survival would increase loss from the pool while production remains fixed. That combination would oppose, rather than explain, the observed increase in platelet count.
options.misconception: Predicts count recovery from shorter platelet survival while holding production fixed.

options.label: B
options.text: Longer platelet survival; reduced platelet production
options.explanation: Longer survival fits reduced destruction, but lower production is not part of the stated selective effect. The model explicitly isolates immune suppression without changing platelet production.
options.misconception: Adds reduced production to a model that changes immune destruction without changing platelet production.

options.label: C
options.text: Shorter platelet survival; increased platelet production
options.explanation: Increased production could introduce a separate explanation for count recovery, but it violates the controlled model. The specified intervention instead reduces immune-mediated platelet loss.
options.misconception: Introduces increased production and shorter survival instead of the stated selective reduction in immune loss.

options.label: D
options.text: Unchanged platelet survival; increased platelet production
options.explanation: This attributes the response to a production change that the model excludes. The proposed corticosteroid pathway preserves the platelet pool by reducing immune destruction instead.
options.misconception: Attributes count recovery to increased production even though the model explicitly holds production constant.

options.label: E
options.text: Longer platelet survival; unchanged platelet production
options.explanation: Suppressing immune-mediated platelet destruction allows platelets to remain available longer. With production fixed by the model, increased survival explains the rise in the circulating count.
options.misconception: No misconception: Reduced immune destruction prolongs platelet survival and raises the pool with production fixed.

context: Learning objective: Separate a fall in platelet destruction from increased production when interpreting immune treatment. With production held constant, longer survival can raise the circulating platelet pool.
